_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `Generation3dMutation` is a semio-NATIVE vocabulary carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no oracle is registered and the decision below records what stands in for one.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.procedural.generation3d` document and all fourteen typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-procedural-3d-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` (the two halves), rules 1, 2, 3 and 4 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md`, and the fourteen committed `(before, mutation, diff, outcome, after)` quintets — which are the only statement of four things: that this subset tags its mutations EXTERNALLY, the payload being `{"CreateWidget": {…}}` with a PascalCase variant name as its single key; that `delete-widget` does NOT cascade, leaving both the synapse that named the widget and its layout entry standing, which is why the layout map has its own `delete-widget-position` verb; that `create-generation` appends AND selects; and that `delete-generation` falls back to the first remaining generation when the one it removed was selected. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `procedural-3d-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument — that the document being a COMPOSITION of two unrelated halves, so that every kind lands in exactly one of two top-level fields, "is this subset's own specification, not a fact an external node-graph library could confirm or refute" — was refuted in this same wave by `mutate-fem2d-1`, `mutate-fem3d-1` and `mutate-gismap-1`, which took Python second implementations over this same carrier. A THIRD-PARTY library was declined, not merely absent: no node-graph format models a graph whose layout is a SPARSE side table keyed by node id and whose document's second half is an unrelated parameter history, and none of them reads this carrier. ALL FOURTEEN KINDS ARE ADJUDICATED AND NONE IS REFUSED: this document holds no composed child, so nothing here depends on a content-addressing function no specification states. A SIBLING NOTE, because the count of second implementations must not be overstated: this reference and `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🌀️procedural/🗿️artifacts/🌀️generation2d/🧪️tests/mutate-procedural-2d-1/🐍️component.py` are ONE implementation instantiated twice — the two documents are the same shape and the two vocabularies differ only in three kind names and four argument names, which is precisely what both no-oracle decisions called the specification. TWO DIVERGENCES THE PAIR SURFACED by being written side by side: `delete-widget` raises `mutation.cascade` at level `info` in `mutate-procedural-2d-1` and raises NOTHING in `mutate-procedural-3d-1`, for an effect that is byte-for-byte identical in both committed vectors; and `s.procedural.generation2d` spells one argument `question_id` in snake_case, the only snake_case identifier in either document model, where its sibling spells it `questionId`. ONE CEILING ON WHAT THIS COMPARISON ESTABLISHES: the SUBJECT half does not run this subset's codec — `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-procedural-3d-1/🦀️.rs` links no plugin crate and replays the committed vectors — so today it establishes that an independent implementation of the specification computes the committed after-snapshots, not yet our codec against a second producer. A `generation3d_mutation_report_json` bridge beside the mutation enum closes it; it is not added here for two reasons, and neither is that the verb is hard: it is PRODUCTION code in a crate this test-side pass deliberately does not touch, and it could not be verified end to end today anyway. `parity` was not measured for any case in this pass: the single-case probe `parity exhaustive --owner 🗒️note --case mutate-note-1` was killed at the runner's OWN 900 s per-case budget while still COMPILING the generated subject host — the runner's message names the cause, shared cargo target-dir lock contention from a concurrent session — and then threw `spawnSync cargo ETIMEDOUT` out of `runProbe` with no summary line at all. `📓️w14-final-audit.md` §5.3 measured the underlying blocker one day earlier (`unresolved import component::component_persistent_local` in `semio-framework-plugin`, which sits in every generated host's dependency graph); this pass did NOT re-verify whether that is still the state, and says so rather than repeating it as fact. This subset's own plugin crate compiles clean at `cargo check --lib`. This case also reads no real-world artifact: all 70 of its fixtures are handcrafted specification vectors. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `procedural-3d-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 14-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

[2026-09-02, D1 — SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION] Promoted from cross-semio-implementation to verified-native-second-implementation: this artifact is semio-native (isSemioNativeArtifact), this reference's own third-party survey above (kept verbatim) already names what was checked and declined, its python implementation differs from the Rust subject, and it covers 100% of this manifest's 1 capability/capabilities with 14 committed fixture vector(s). See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️d1-native-oracle-discharge.md.

candidatesConsidered.reason: no node-graph format models a graph whose layout is a SPARSE side table keyed by node id and whose document's second half is an unrelated parameter history, and none of them reads this carrier.

oracles.rationale: 🧊️ The third-party half that touches REAL KERNEL OUTPUT. `🧪️tests/📐️example-geometry-3d-1/🥒️.feature`'s subject, `📚️examples/🧪️tests/🧩️geometry/🦀️.rs`, evaluates each of the eight bundled examples' own `🗣️.dsl.semio` through the real `FlowHost` with the packaged `brep`/`math` flow extensions installed and tessellates the preview handle through the same `tessellate_geometry` bridge the editor's preview path calls; `parry3d` then recomputes that triangle soup's volume and centre of mass (`MassProperties::from_trimesh`) and its axis-aligned bounding box (`TriMesh::local_aabb`) with code this repository did not write, and the lane asserts BOTH numbers against the committed `🧪️tests/🧩️example/🔣️.json` expectation. `parry3d` sits on no exact-geometry kernel (`engine.family = "none"`): it is a mesh/collision library, so its independence from the `semio-s-artifact-stdio-semio` B-Rep kernel under test is total, and it is already carried at exactly this standing — `[dev-dependencies]` only, never `[dependencies]`, never production-reachable — by `🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🧊️3d`. ⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT ESTABLISH, stated so the count of evidence is not overstated: `parry3d` measures whatever soup it is handed and cannot tell a correct solid from a wrong one, so it is PAIRED with, never substituted for, the committed expectation that `example-geometry-scipy` derives independently. The two together are what closes the case: `scipy` says what the number must be, `parry3d` says what the kernel actually produced, and the fixture is the single file both are held to.

packages.role: array algebra the quadrature integrands are evaluated over

oracles.rationale: 📐️ The third-party half that states WHAT THE NUMBER MUST BE, independently of any semio code. `🧪️tests/📐️example-geometry-3d-1/🐍️.py` reads exactly two committed, language-neutral inputs — each example's own `🗣️.dsl.semio` (for its wired slider values and its declared `neuron-kind` chain) and the packaged brep extension descriptor `✏️s/🔌️plugins/🌊️flow/🧩️extensions/📐️brep/🔣️.json` (for the channel defaults an unwired port falls back to, which is how `🍩️sphere-cut-with-torus`'s torus gets its major/minor radii) — and re-derives every expected number in all eight `🧪️tests/🧩️example/🔣️.json` fixtures. It imports nothing from this repository and evaluates no graph: it recognises each op chain as the classical solid it is and integrates that solid. Six of the eight are closed form (rectangular prism twice, regular-polygon prism, hollow box, rounded box as the Minkowski sum of a shrunk cube with a ball); the two that are not are integrated with `scipy.integrate.quad` — the ball∪cube union over clipped disc areas, and the ball∖torus difference over the torus tube angle. ⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT ESTABLISH: it never touches the kernel, so it can only convict a wrong FIXTURE, never a wrong SOLID; a disagreement located here is a fixture error and a disagreement located in the Rust lane is a kernel error. That half is `example-geometry-parry3d`. 📌️ A THIRD, NON-ORACLE CONFIRMATION, recorded so the evidence is not miscounted as three references: the TypeScript lane (`📚️examples/<example>/🧪️tests/🧩️example/🟦️.ts`) repeats both quadratures with its own composite-Simpson rule and recomputes every closed-form value, so the two integrated volumes rest on two independent quadrature implementations rather than one library — but that lane is this repository's own code and contributes no third-party independence.

engine.implementation: scipy.integrate.quad adaptive quadrature over analytic solid cross-sections

oracles.rationale: 🔺️ The QUALIFYING third-party half of this subset's IO surface. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END found that seven of this artifact's nine format leaves were placeholders that could not fail: export returned `print_dsl(snapshot).into_bytes()` — the artifact's own DSL text — under the target format's name (byte-identical bodies for las, png, stl, dwg, obj, gltf and ply), and import did `let _ = bytes; Ok(Generation3dSnapshot::default())`, discarding the file for an EMPTY document. Neither direction ever raised an error. The lane registered here, `[[test]] io-round-trip` at `🚪️io/🧪️tests/🔁️round-trip/🦀️.rs`, drives ONE committed geometry (`🧫️fixtures/🚪️io/🧊️unit-cube/🔣️.json`: 8 shared vertices, 12 triangles, bounds [0,0,0]..[1,1,1], enclosed volume exactly 1.0) out through every real export leaf and back in through every real import leaf, and hands every RECOVERED mesh to `parry3d::mass_properties::MassProperties::from_trimesh` and `parry3d::bounding_volume::Aabb::from_points`. What parry3d contributes is the number no assertion of ours can supply on its own: the enclosed volume. A codec that dropped a face, reversed a winding or collapsed an axis moves that number and does not necessarily move a triangle count, which is exactly the class of silent corruption the placeholders' replacement has to be held to. parry3d shares no code with this repository's mesh path and is already a registered test-only dependency of this subset (see `example-geometry-parry3d`, which uses the same library on kernel output rather than on codec output — the two lanes are independent and are both kept). COVERAGE, stated rather than implied: the third-party check runs on the six formats whose export leaves produce geometry — stl, obj, ply, gltf, dwg and (as a point cloud, so bounds only, no volume) las. `txt` is this artifact's own full-fidelity DSL text and is round-tripped by value equality instead, `json` was already real before this ticket, and `png` is generation2d's export claim and refuses in both directions here. NETWORK: none; the library is vendored through the workspace lock like every other test-lane dependency.

🚪️ The SUPPLEMENTAL, cross-LANGUAGE half of the same IO surface, at `🧪️tests/🚪️io-procedural-3d-1/🐍️.py`: an independent Python implementation of the three text mesh grammars this artifact writes and reads — ASCII STL, Wavefront OBJ and ASCII PLY — written from the format specifications and from `🧫️fixtures/🚪️io/🧊️unit-cube/🔣️.json`, importing nothing from this repository's Rust. It writes the committed cube in each grammar, reads it back, and projects triangle count, vertex count, bounds and enclosed volume; the committed `🧫️fixtures/🚪️io/🧊️unit-cube/*second-implementation.*` files ARE its output, and `[[test]] io-round-trip` feeds exactly those files through this artifact's real import leaves — so the two implementations meet on both sides of the boundary rather than only agreeing about a number. WHY IT IS REGISTERED AS SUPPLEMENTAL AND NOT AS QUALIFYING, stated plainly: STL, OBJ and PLY are not semio-native formats and real third-party readers for all three exist and are already registered by their owning stdio subsets (`stl_io`, `tobj`, `ply-rs`), so `verified-native-second-implementation` would be an unearned claim here. The qualifying third-party oracle for `procedural-3d-1-io` is `io-round-trip-parry3d`, registered beside this entry. What this entry adds that no library in the subject's own ecosystem can is a reader written in ANOTHER LANGUAGE from the specification by an implementer who did not read our writer — the one shape of evidence that separates 'the codec works' from 'our reader accepts our writer'. CEILING: the SUBJECT half of that case (`🦀️.rs` beside the reference) does not run this artifact's codec, because a generated test host may not link a plugin crate; it replays the committed vector and checks only container magic and per-triangle record counts. The codec itself is exercised against the same bytes by the in-crate `io-round-trip` lane. SCOPE: only the three text grammars are adjudicated cross-language — `gltf` and `dwg` are container formats a page of Python could only re-implement as a worse copy of the artifact's own codec, and `las` is export-only for this artifact by design; all three are covered by the parry3d lane instead. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

engine.implementation: in-repository second implementation of the ascii stl, wavefront obj and ascii ply grammars
